mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers equity discount rates and stimulates corporate investment.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly non-farm payrolls increase exceeding 100,000 jobs triggers positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days by signaling robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS monthly change exceeds 100.0, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rising retail sales (RSAFS) and falling industrial production (INDPRO) indicate demand-driven economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as corporate profit outlook deteriorates.
failure_condition: When RSAFS rises and INDPRO falls, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that triggers Federal Reserve rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate leverage.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 5.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) consistently predict positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as stronger consumer spending directly supports corporate revenue growth and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: RSAFS shows positive monthly change but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline exceeding 0.5% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profitability and investment confidence.
failure_condition: When INDPRO monthly change is below -0.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rising unemployment (UNRATE increase > 0.2%) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signal weak economic conditions with accommodative policy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as stimulus expectations rise.
failure_condition: When UNRATE increases > 0.2% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as stronger manufacturing output supports economic growth, corporate earnings, and investor confidence in cyclical sectors.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows positive monthly change but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.
